oh_bulbster_boulder_the.blurb: A small bouldering spot on the Elywood side of the river at Cascade and Elywood Park, in the Lorain and Elyria area of northern Ohio. It is one of several little sectors scattered around the park, reached on foot from the Cascade Park playground end. The problems run from easy up to around V5, with most of them landing between V1 and V2, so it suits a short session for climbers at a range of levels. It is a low-key, tucked-away area that sees few visitors, though it is not completely secluded. Bring pads and plan on a quick visit rather than a full day.

oh_dad_s_wall_aka_glass_buttress.blurb: A compact wall in the southeast section of Mad River Gorge near Springfield, Ohio, with eleven climbs of mixed type: mostly trad, a few sport lines, one top rope and a single boulder problem. Most routes are moderate, from 5.5 to 5.7, with a small cluster around 5.10 for stronger climbers and one V3 traverse. The arete near the start holds a popular easy sport lead that makes a good first lead for newer climbers, and the lines here reportedly stay dry after rain. The gorge is the largest climbing area in the state and can draw a crowd.

oh_baseball_field.blurb: A short cliff line behind the outfield of a ballfield near the dam at Lake Vesuvius, in the Ironton Unit of Wayne National Forest in southern Ohio. Eleven routes mix sport, top rope and trad, mostly between 5.6 and 5.7, with a handful easier at 5.5 or harder up to about 5.10. Walls around the lake are generally low, topping out at roughly 35 to 40 feet, and most of the lakeside rock sits in shade, which helps in summer. It is a friendly, uncomplicated spot for beginners and for quick top-rope laps, right beside the field.

oh_2_left_main_wall.blurb: A sandstone face in the old quarry at Big Cliffs, within Logtown Stone Quarry County Park in northeast Ohio. Eleven routes, almost all bolted sport lines with a single trad line, follow the drill marks left by the quarrymen. The grades lean hard: a few lines from 5.8 to 5.10, then the bulk between 5.11 and 5.13, which makes this one of the steeper-graded walls of the cliff. The rock is better low down and loose near the top, so watch for debris overhead. Expect a short stair-and-trail walk from the car.
oh_2_left_main_wall.approach: From the lot, follow the bike trail to the climber sign and go up the stone steps. Turn left along the fence to its end, then turn right up more steps to the cliff. Bear left; the wall is on your right, with a hollow or pond on the left.

oh_commitment_boulder.blurb: A small cluster of boulder problems in the Trailer Park Boulders zone near Athens, in southeast Ohio, close to Stroud's Run. It centers on a colonnade tucked into an alcove, and many of the eleven problems start around it. Grades are concentrated at V3, with a few V2s and a couple of tougher lines near V6. It makes a sensible stop for a boulderer already working the neighboring Athens blocs. Bring pads.
